Sean / team,

Thanks for the ping and attaching the client's mark-up. I've reviewed Novum's redlines and drafted recommended positions and two alternative clause sets we can propose back. High level: we should offer a clear, marketable compromise that preserves our ability to improve the service while giving Novum contractual assurances about customer data and outputs. Below are the suggested points and language snippets you can send to Olivia.

1) Output ownership (customer-generated outputs) — proposed approach:
- Customer gets a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, transferrable right to use Outputs ("Customer Outputs") produced by the Service using Customer Content. Redwood does not claim ownership of Customer Outputs.
- Draft (client-friendly): "Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content and Customer Outputs. Redwood hereby assigns to Customer any right, title and interest it may have in Customer Outputs, and grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Customer Outputs for any purpose."
- Draft (balanced/product-friendly): "Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Content. For clarity, Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to use Customer Outputs. Redwood reserves no ownership claim over Customer Outputs but may use de-identified aggregate outputs for service improvement."

2) Training on customer data (core ask) — proposed approach: opt-in by default with an explicit order form checkbox plus a defined scope and retention window if enabled.
- Redwood position: we will not use Customer Content to train or fine-tune models unless Customer explicitly opts in via the Order Form or an addendum. If opted-in, Redwood will only use Content in accordance with the agreed scope and will implement agreed anonymization safeguards and retention limits.
- Draft clause: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune or otherwise update model weights or supervised training datasets without Customer's prior written consent provided in the applicable Order Form. If Customer provides such consent, the Parties shall agree the scope, duration and technical safeguards (including anonymization and deletion timelines) in the Order Form or a mutually-executed addendum."

3) Feedback / telemetry license — proposed approach: narrow, non-exclusive license for improvements and fixes; prefer anonymized/aggregate telemetry and explicit exclusions for Customer Confidential Information and Protected Data.
- Draft clause: "Customer hereby grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Feedback (defined as usage analytics, anonymized performance metrics and non-identifying telemetry) solely to operate, maintain and improve Redwood's services (including model research). Feedback shall not include Customer Confidential Information or any Protected Data. Redwood shall not use identifiable Customer Content for model training absent consent per the Training clause above."

4) Commercial trade-offs to offer Novum (negotiation levers):
- If Novum requires a strict 'no training' stance, offer a pricing discount or service credit in exchange for restricting service-improvement usage of telemetry for a defined period.
- Alternatively, offer opt-in training at a lower per-token price and a defined deletion/retention schedule (e.g., retention for 90 days post ingestion, deletion thereafter).

5) Next steps / redline delivery: I've prepared a one-page tracked-changes redline (Redwood_proposed_clause_draft.docx) with the two drafting options inline. Recommend we send the balanced/product-friendly language first and mark the training clause as "Option A (No training) / Option B (Opt-in training with safeguards)" so Novum can choose.

If the customer pushes on assignment language for Outputs (they asked for assignment), we should aim for the license approach. Assignments can be problematic for our IP insurance and platform-level ownership of derivative research. If execs want to push harder on assignment, let me know and I will flag for GC escalation.

I'll be available for a 30-minute sync with Procurement/legal if they'd like to walk through the options.
